report.quality_note: Parse/type validation is not semantic ground truth or measured link precision.

blocking_issues: The mapping emits both `entity.abn` and `entity.acn` from every nonempty `AFS_LIC_ABN_ACN` value. The source documentation explicitly says this column contains an ABN if one was provided, otherwise an ACN; it does not identify its type per row. A validator may suppress values failing the respective checksum, but the supplied mapping has no documented mutually exclusive, type-discriminating condition. As configured, a value that happens to validate under both schemes could be asserted as both identifiers, and the mapping's claim that validation distinguishes types is not supported by the declarative `when` clauses shown. This must be made type-exclusive (or the mixed identifier left unmapped) before approval.
warnings: The mapping correctly treats the row as an AFS licence-register entry for a licence holder, not as a branch, condition, prior licence, or reporting group. However, the canonical subset has no licence object/identifier field, so `AFS_LIC_NUM` remains only provenance rather than a mapped licence claim. This is an acceptable disclosed limitation.

`AFS_LIC_NAME` is appropriately not emitted as `entity.legal_name` or `entity.trading_name`: documentation calls it a register-entry name and allows either an individual name or organisation name. Retaining it only as a noncanonical subject label avoids an unsupported legal-name assertion.
The mapping correctly does not map `AFS_LIC_START_DT` to `entity.date_registered`; it is the licence/licensee start date, not evidence of entity incorporation or registration.

No entity status is asserted. Inclusion in a snapshot of current AFS licensees supports current register inclusion/licensing context only, not company legal status. The limitation is correctly disclosed.

Address mappings are semantically aligned with documentation: component fields describe the current principal business address. `address_role: business` is reasonably supported as a label, provided it is not interpreted as a branch/service location or a full street address. Documentation warns blank components can mean an unvalidated supplied address; this is disclosed. No full address is invented.

`AFS_LIC_ADD_COUNTRY` is raw source text, with foreign countries represented as `International`, not a standard country value. Leaving the raw text as `address.country` is traceable but has reduced semantic precision for non-Australian rows; it must not be normalized to `AU` or another specific country without evidence.

The documentation describes a point-in-time weekly snapshot, but no row-level snapshot timestamp is supplied. Using CKAN resource last-modified as `observed_at` is acceptable only as the clearly labelled publication proxy shown; it must not be read as a per-record statement/change time. The naive timestamp's UTC assumption is also disclosed rather than sourced.

Source reliability and field-confidence values are explicitly uncalibrated judgements. Values around 0.9 should not be interpreted as measured accuracy; the mapping appropriately labels them provisional, though the identifier-field confidence should be revisited after the blocking identifier fix.

The sample and exploration show AFS licence numbers are nonempty and unique in the examined 300 rows, supporting their provenance use, but this is discovery evidence rather than a guarantee for all releases. The documentation's uniqueness statement is the stronger basis.

Conditions and pre-FSR licences are correctly left unmapped. Their serialized multi-value/text formats and lack of corresponding fields mean no normalized permission, historic/current licence, or entity assertion should be inferred.
evidence_checked: ASIC Help File p.3: dataset is a point-in-time snapshot containing publicly available information for current AFS licensees.

ASIC Help File p.8: `AFS_LIC_NUM` is the unique AFS-licensee identifier; `AFS_LIC_NAME` is a register-entry name that may be an individual's given/family names or an organisation name; `AFS_LIC_ABN_ACN` is ABN when supplied, otherwise ACN, or null.

ASIC Help File pp.9-10: address components are from the current principal business address, and blanks may reflect an address that could not be validated; foreign country values are represented as `International`.
ASIC Help File p.11: `AFS_LIC_CONDITION` contains current authorised services/products in two serialized output formats.

Discovery evidence: examined 300 records had nonempty, unique `AFS_LIC_NUM`; all 300 condition fields used tilde serialization; 28 pre-FSR values used tilde serialization; the displayed rows contain 11-digit mixed-identifier values and address components consistent with the documented fields.

Previous mapping and validation output: fields emitted are identifier/address only; name, start date, conditions, prior licences, and register name are explicitly unmapped; output labels resource timestamp as a publication proxy.

blocking_issues: The proposed mapping is semantically unsafe if it emits both `entity.abn` and `entity.acn` from `AFS_LIC_ABN_ACN`. ASIC documents this as a mixed field: show ABN if supplied; otherwise show ACN; otherwise null. No per-row type discriminator is present. Checksum validation alone is not a documented mutually exclusive mapping condition, and the displayed declarative mapping has no such exclusive condition. The field must remain unmapped or be routed through a demonstrably type-exclusive discriminator before human approval.
warnings: Row grain is correctly understood as one current, point-in-time AFS licence-register entry for a licence holder, rather than a condition, prior licence, branch, service location, legal entity, or reporting group. `AFS_LIC_NUM` is a licence identifier and cannot be promoted to an entity identifier; retaining it only in provenance is an acceptable ontology limitation.

It is correct not to map `AFS_LIC_NAME` to legal or trading name. The help file calls it a register-entry name and expressly permits individual or organisation names. This source provides no basis for legal-name, trading-name, entity-type, or historical-name assertions.
It is correct not to map the AFS start date to entity registration/incorporation date. It is licence/licensee timing, not entity registration timing.
No legal-entity status is asserted, correctly. Current inclusion in this AFS-licensee snapshot does not establish active company status, deregistration, liquidation, or suspension.

Mapped locality, state, postcode, and country are supported as components of the current principal business address. `address_role: business` is reasonable only if consumers do not reinterpret it as registered office, branch, or service location. No street/full address is available. Blank values can reflect failure to validate an address, as disclosed.

Country is source text. ASIC represents addresses outside Australia as `International`, so it must not be standardized into a particular country or the ontology default AU. Mapping raw country text is partial and should retain this limitation.

The source has no row-level observed/change/snapshot timestamp. CKAN last-modified may be used only as the clearly labelled publication proxy shown, not as when the individual record or address was stated/changed. UTC for a timezone-naive proxy is an implementation assumption, not source evidence.

The uncalibrated source-reliability and field-confidence scores are disclosed appropriately and should not be read as measured correctness. Address confidence is broadly plausible, but it does not repair the mixed-identifier issue.

Leaving conditions and pre-FSR values unmapped is appropriate: they are serialized licence-related values, may be multi-valued, and the supplied ontology has no matching licence/permission/history fields.
evidence_checked: ASIC Help File p.3: the dataset is a point-in-time snapshot of public information for current AFS licensees.

ASIC Help File p.8: AFS licence number is a unique licence/licensee identifier; register-entry name may be an individual or organisation; the mixed ABN/ACN field supplies ABN if available, otherwise ACN.
ASIC Help File pp.9-10: fields are components of the current principal business address; blank address fields can mean unvalidated input; foreign addresses are represented as International.
ASIC Help File p.11: conditions are current licence authorisations in two serialized formats.

Discovery evidence: reviewed rows exhibit nonempty unique licence numbers in the sampled 300 records, 11-digit mixed identifiers in examples, address components, and serialized tilde-delimited conditions/prior licences.
Proposed mapping/validation: it deliberately leaves name, licence start date, conditions, prior licences, and register name unmapped; it labels the resource timestamp as a publication proxy.
